newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Treasury posts record gap in 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Treasury posts record gap in 1996 - paper.

text.p: Brazil's National Treasury had a record deficit of about 9.0 billion reais in 1996 as a result of higher interest rate expenses and financing and personnel costs, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said.
Gazeta, citing central bank estimates, said the failure to control federal expenses helped boost the total public sector operating deficit in 1996 to 4.78 percent of gross domestic product.
Despite higher revenues and a freeze on public workers' salaries, the primary deficit worsened, it said.
Federal government expenses reached roughly 107 billion reais while revenues reached only 98 billion reais last year, the paper said.

The government in December raked in a record 10.3 billion reais in revenues but the treasury still ended the month with a 1.5 billion-real deficit due to federal payroll expenses and payments of interest on internal and external public debt, it said.
Only to meet obligations to the Paris Club, the treasury paid out 829.8 million reais, it added.
